lines.text: Hi, I'm Sindy! Let's bring CVMFS software into a sind cluster.
Your jobs load their software from CVMFS. So how do you get it onto every node of a test cluster?
sind covers two use cases. Consume it, so jobs read from it, or provision it, to test the tooling that installs the client.
To consume it, set the cvmfs flag in the storage section. The nodes need no extra privileges.
If the client runs on your host, check its mount first. Here it's shared, the default on systemd hosts.
Next, create the cluster from that file.
And sind tries the mount before it creates any node, so a broken setup fails early.
sind picks the backend: a Docker volume plugin named cvmfs if one is installed, otherwise the mount on the host.
Every node gets it read-only, including workers added later. Repositories appear on first access, so there's no list to configure.
To test your provisioning instead, leave storage unset, and let the client run inside the nodes.
Those nodes need an extra capability and the fuse device, and on AppArmor hosts, an unconfined profile.
In short: one setting mounts CVMFS on every node, sind picks the backend, and provisioning tests run the client inside the nodes.
Next up: users and identity. See you there!
